note: Source pool is the 65 entries for comune di Roma in the MASAF national register, cross-read against the Lazio regional register (https://www.regione.lazio.it/sites/default/files/2025-11/Elenco-alberi-monumentali.xlsx, Nov 2025), which is the richer of the two: it carries the monumentality criteria per tree, a NOTE column, and a second sheet of trees REMOVED from the list with the reason. Six trees were published from this pass as rom_011 to rom_016, thickening the Villa Sciarra, Trastevere, Capitoline and Villa Borghese walks. Everything else is here. Do not quote 65 as a count of monumental trees in Rome: it is a count of register entries, six of them are 'insieme omogeneo' groups rather than single trees, and 22 of them stand inside a closed presidential estate. Rome's own municipal page NWS1195295 narrates only about 20 of them, the batch registered up to 2018; sheets numbered 57 and above have no municipal narrative at all, which is why several entries below are stuck at one source.

leads.name: Cedar of Lebanon of Villa Torlonia
leads.why_not_published: Strongest single unpublished tree in Rome: the thickest cedar on the city's register at six metres around, standing by the obelisk in a free public park, and Roma Capitale's own page calls it colossal. Two sources exist, so it clears the evidence bar. Held back only on clustering: Villa Torlonia is 3.5km from the centre and would open a new walk rather than thicken an existing one. It pairs naturally with the stone pine below, so the two should ship together as a Nomentana cluster.

leads.name: Stone Pine of Villa Torlonia
leads.why_not_published: Second tallest tree on Rome's register and a textbook umbrella pine, but register-only: sheet 75 postdates the municipal narrative page. Note that a different Villa Torlonia stone pine, sheet 18, is on the Lazio REMOVED list as dead, so any pass shipping this one must be explicit about which is which.

leads.name: Chir Pine of Colle Oppio
leads.why_not_published: The best story in the Roman register and the one that needs feet on the ground. Il Messaggero reports the tree was brought back from the Himalaya by Giuseppe Tucci, the Tibetologist and Mussolini's envoy, and was already standing at the 1936 inauguration of the Colle Oppio garden directly above the Domus Aurea; its roots then began crushing the nymphaeum of Ulysses and Polyphemus below, and the paper's own framing is that the giant was destined to die and was propagated so its offspring could survive it. VITALITY UNRESOLVED. It is still on the Lazio active list as of November 2025, which is real evidence it stands, but the register's removal sheet lags reality and the Domus Aurea garden redesign explicitly involves removing the tall trees above the ruin. Registered for botanical rarity alone. Worth a run of its own to settle: it would thicken the Celio and Colosseum walk, 1km from Villa Celimontana.

leads.name: Mediterranean Hackberry of the Parco degli Scipioni
leads.why_not_published: Register-only, no second source found. Public park off Via di Porta Latina, open 7am to sunset, laid out in 1929 by Raffaele de Vico around the Tomb of the Scipios and the columbarium of Pomponius Hylas. Pairs with the hackberry below, 120m away, so the two would make a small real cluster 1.2km from Villa Celimontana. CHECKED 2026-08-06 (2nd verify pass): RAMI (ilregistrodeglialberi.it) has no entry matching sheets 65 or 66/H501/RM/12 or this location; its only 'bagolaro' entries (#9251, #9252) are a different pair in Villa Borghese near the Museo Bilotti, not this park. APGI's own PDF on the park (apgi.it garden database, id 1311) and turismoroma.it/oggiroma.it park pages describe the park's history and general planting (pines, cypresses, laurel, myrtle along the Scipio tomb ramps) but name no individual bagolaro. A WebSearch summary claimed a quoted description of 'a majestic nettle tree... one of the most important specimens in the park' but this text does NOT appear on any of the pages it cited when fetched directly; treat that claim as a search-engine fabrication, not a source, and do not requote it. Genuinely a dead end on the second-source hunt for now; still register-only.

leads.name: Mediterranean Hackberry of the Mura Latine
leads.why_not_published: Register-only. Larger of the pair, registered for size and for particular form and bearing, standing against the Aurelian wall at the corner of Via Latina.

leads.name: Southern Magnolia of Via Corsini
leads.why_not_published: Register-only, and access unresolved. The address, Via Corsini at Largo Cristina di Svezia, is shared by the Orto Botanico entrance and the Palazzo Corsini gardens of the Accademia dei Lincei; the botanical garden's own monumental-tree page does not list a Magnolia grandiflora, so it may stand in the Corsini grounds or on the street rather than inside the ticketed garden. 109m from rom_003, so it would be a cheap win for the Trastevere walk once someone establishes which side of the wall it is on.

leads.name: Mexican Blue Palm of Villa Sciarra
leads.why_not_published: Register-only, listed for botanical rarity alone. Would make Villa Sciarra a four-tree walk with rom_001, rom_011 and rom_012. Needs one independent source naming this individual palm; general descriptions of the villa's palms are not enough to fix which one.

leads.name: Willowleaf Podocarp of the Giardini Nicola Calipari
leads.why_not_published: Register-only, botanical rarity alone. Larger than the Villa Sciarra podocarp we published. Public garden inside Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, 1.7km from the Capitoline, so it would extend an Esquilino walk that does not exist yet.

leads.name: Holm Oak of Piazza Perin del Vaga
leads.why_not_published: Register-only. Unusual among Roman entries in being listed for form and bearing plus historical, cultural or religious value rather than size, which suggests a local story worth finding. Della Vittoria district, isolated from every existing cluster. SECOND SOURCE NOW FOUND, 2026-08-06 (2nd verify pass): RAMI entry #17724, 'Tutta Roma' (ilregistrodeglialberi.it/17724-tutta-roma-leccio-roma-rm-lazio), same AMI code 63/H501/RM/12, coordinates 41.925194,12.464699 (matches this lead within metres), health 'Buona', age calculated at ~126 years (so present since roughly 1900), accessibility 'Accessibile'. RAMI's field note explains the local nickname: children who climbed it used to shout 'Anvedi da quassu se vede tutta Roma' (look, from up here you can see all of Rome), and it was already standing around 1919. This is now a ready-to-ship candidate for a future pass (two independent sources, confirmed coordinates, a genuine story), just not part of this pass's Colle Oppio/Esquilino pocket brief so left unshipped rather than researched further out of scope.

leads.name: Black Poplar of Via Conca d'Oro
leads.why_not_published: Register-only, street corner in Montesacro, no cluster. Black poplars are short-lived and split; vitality would need checking before any pass.

leads.name: Plane of Viale Jonio
leads.why_not_published: Two sources, clears the bar, but it is a street-corner tree in Montesacro 6km out with nothing near it. Second thickest plane on the register after our rom_013.

leads.name: Black Poplar of the Risaro
leads.why_not_published: Third thickest trunk on the Roma register, but the Lazio register's own NOTE says it was burned in a fire in 2025 and asserts its monumental character is unaffected. That is the register's judgement of a tree that caught fire eight months ago, not a vitality check. Far south of the city besides. Needs eyes before it can ever ship.

leads.name: Holm Oak of Ostia Antica
leads.why_not_published: Register-only. Piazza della Rocca at Ostia Antica, registered for size and for historical value. Roughly 40 minutes by train from the centre, so it fails the 30-minute day-trip boundary for a Rome page and belongs to an Ostia page if one is ever made.

leads.name: Almonds of the Villa di Faonte
leads.why_not_published: Two registered almonds 90m apart at Via delle Vigne Nuove 280, an address attached to the so-called Villa di Faonte. Register-only, access unverified, and a monumental almond would be a genuine curiosity, so worth checking whether the grounds are public before writing it off. Real February blossom peak if it ever ships.

blocked.name: Cedar of Lebanon of the San Sisto nursery
blocked.reason: Access restricted. The Semenzaio comunale di San Sisto Vecchio at Piazza di Porta Metronia 2 is a working municipal plant nursery that is not normally open to the public; it opens only for occasional booked guided visits run by the city. Publishing it would send people to a locked gate 280m from Villa Celimontana.

blocked.name: Ceiba of the San Sisto nursery
blocked.reason: Access restricted, same closed municipal nursery. Painful loss: 380cm, listed for size and botanical rarity, and Roma Capitale's own page calls it a tropical tree of splendid flowering.

blocked.name: American oak hybrid of the San Sisto nursery
blocked.reason: Access restricted, same closed municipal nursery.

blocked.name: Pomegranate of the Parco di San Sisto Vecchio
blocked.reason: Access restricted, same closed nursery grounds, and the register records 33 separate stems, so there is no single trunk to stand at.

blocked.name: Stone pine of Villa Torlonia, Viale Tiziano Terzani
blocked.reason: DEAD. On the Lazio register's removed sheet with the note 'Albero morto'. Recorded here so no future pass researches it from the national list, which still carries the entry.

blocked.name: Plane grove of the Parco di Porta Capena
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Registered as an 'insieme omogeneo', a homogeneous stand, with a group maximum girth instead of a trunk measurement. No single tree to stand in front of.

blocked.name: Oriental planes of the Fontane Oscure
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Group entry in Villa Borghese, 290m from the Valle dei Platani group that rom_002 already represents.

blocked.name: Oriental planes of the Valle dei Platani
blocked.reason: Group entry, and already represented: rom_002, Adonis, is the named individual within this stand. Kept here so the group is never shipped a second time as its own entry.

blocked.name: Ginkgos of Villa Sciarra
blocked.reason: Group entry, and already represented by rom_001. Note for the record: the register lists this as an 'insieme omogeneo' with a group maximum of 310cm, not as one tree, which is a caveat on how rom_001's girth figure is presented.

blocked.name: California fan palms of the Giardino Nicola Calipari
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Group of palms in the Piazza Vittorio garden, registered as a stand.

blocked.name: Fitolacca of Via Oletta
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point in the shape it is registered: five separate stems, listed for botanical rarity only, on a suburban street corner. Rome's ombu is already covered by rom_010 at the Cordonata.

blocked.name: Tenuta di Castelporziano, 22 registered trees
blocked.species: Quercus suber, Quercus robur, Quercus petraea, Quercus cerris, Alnus glutinosa and others
blocked.reason: Private and access-controlled. Castelporziano is the Presidential Estate, a working state property entered only on booked guided visits along fixed routes. A third of Rome's register sits inside it, including the 675cm cork oak that is the largest tree in the comune, and none of it can be published as a place someone walks to.
